request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 35.0% (95% band 30.6% to 38.0%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.283: -0.66; 0.283 <= x < 0.46: -0.31; 0.46 <= x < 0.606: +0.06; 0.606 <= x < 0.654: +0.7; 0.654 <= x < 0.689: +1.2; 0.689 <= x < 0.731: +1.7; 0.731 <= x < 0.809: +2.5; x >= 0.809: +3.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.05, 95% band [+2.84, +3.35]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 20.7% (95% band 18.1% to 22.1%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.6 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.94, 95% band [+0.85, +1.02]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 10.5% (95% band 8.4% to 11.6%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 33,200: +0.31; 33,200 <= x < 53,600: +0.06; 53,600 <= x < 76,800: -0.1; x >= 76,800: -0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.76, 95% band [-0.86, -0.59]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 8.8% (95% band 7.1% to 9.7%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 101: +0.25; 101 <= x < 277: -0.0333; x >= 277: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.56, 95% band [-0.70, -0.45]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 7.7% (95% band 5.6% to 8.2%); rank 4 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.431: -0.1; x >= 0.431: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.38, 95% band [+0.25, +0.43]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 3.3% (95% band 1.7% to 4.2%); rank 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1: -0.05; >= 2: +0.07 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.22, 95% band [+0.10, +0.30]).
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.2% to 2.2%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.07, +0.11]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.3% (95% band 0.1% to 1.9%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.00, 95% band [-0.14, +0.03]).
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 0.1% (95% band 0.1% to 2.0%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.04, +0.10]).

Interactions: the model has 30 pairs. The larger ones:
- `n_delinquencies & dti`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.4% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.96 (95% band +0.82 to +1.03) when `dti` = 0.0307, +0.86 (95% band +0.68 to +0.97) when `dti` = 0.57.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0307 to 0.57: +0.45 (95% band +0.27 to +0.53) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +0.35 (95% band +0.18 to +0.46) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 1.1% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +3.03 (95% band +2.83 to +3.33) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +3.06 (95% band +2.80 to +3.36) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.95 (95% band +0.77 to +1.13) when `utilization` = 0.0994, +0.97 (95% band +0.71 to +1.17) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `utilization & n_inquiries`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.2% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +3.00 (95% band +2.82 to +3.32) when `n_inquiries` = 0, +3.12 (95% band +2.85 to +3.36) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.11 (95% band +0.04 to +0.28) when `utilization` = 0.0994, +0.23 (95% band +0.09 to +0.33) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `utilization & income`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.9% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +2.88 (95% band +2.76 to +3.27) when `income` = 22,000, +3.05 (95% band +2.82 to +3.40) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.81 (95% band -0.97 to -0.52) when `utilization` = 0.0994, -0.64 (95% band -0.87 to -0.46) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.6% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +3.13 (95% band +2.83 to +3.44) when `history_months` = 24.2, +3.00 (95% band +2.82 to +3.31) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.49 (95% band -0.78 to -0.33) when `utilization` = 0.0994, -0.62 (95% band -0.79 to -0.40) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `n_delinquencies & history_months`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.2% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.89 (95% band +0.79 to +1.01) when `history_months` = 24.2, +0.95 (95% band +0.81 to +1.03) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.60 (95% band -0.76 to -0.45) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.54 (95% band -0.74 to -0.41) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `utilization & dti`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.3% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +3.04 (95% band +2.83 to +3.36) when `dti` = 0.0307, +3.11 (95% band +2.85 to +3.44) when `dti` = 0.57.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0307 to 0.57: +0.37 (95% band +0.20 to +0.50) when `utilization` = 0.0994, +0.44 (95% band +0.22 to +0.58) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `income & history_months`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.4% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.76 (95% band -0.89 to -0.54) when `history_months` = 24.2, -0.76 (95% band -0.90 to -0.55) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.60 (95% band -0.78 to -0.42) when `income` = 22,000, -0.60 (95% band -0.76 to -0.42) when `income` = 114,000.
- `n_delinquencies & income`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.2% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +1.07 (95% band +0.82 to +1.13) when `income` = 22,000, +0.96 (95% band +0.85 to +1.10) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.71 (95% band -0.87 to -0.56) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.81 (95% band -0.87 to -0.50) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `history_months & feature_b`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.60 (95% band -0.74 to -0.44) when `feature_b` = -1.66, -0.52 (95% band -0.65 to -0.41) when `feature_b` = 1.65.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.66 to 1.65: +0.01 (95% band -0.10 to +0.10) when `history_months` = 24.2, +0.09 (95% band -0.07 to +0.18) when `history_months` = 343.
- `income & dti`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.2% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.73 (95% band -0.84 to -0.58) when `dti` = 0.0307, -0.80 (95% band -0.99 to -0.57) when `dti` = 0.57.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0307 to 0.57: +0.46 (95% band +0.21 to +0.55) when `income` = 22,000, +0.39 (95% band +0.15 to +0.44) when `income` = 114,000.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by revolving credit utilization, the share of the credit limit an applicant is using, which accounts for about 35% of its importance."},{"id":2,"text":"Risk rises steeply with utilization: applicants using less than about 46% of their limit carry lower predicted risk, while those above about 73% carry much higher risk, and moving from the 5th to the 95th percentile adds roughly 3 units of log-odds, the largest effect in the model."},{"id":3,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver (about 21%), with predicted risk rising from no delinquencies to two or more, a net change of roughly +0.9 log-odds across the typical range."},{"id":4,"text":"Income, the length of credit history and the debt-to-income ratio have smaller, moderate effects: higher income and longer credit history lower predicted risk, while a debt-to-income ratio above about 0.43 raises it."},{"id":5,"text":"Number of recent credit inquiries, feature_b, age and feature_a have little or no resolved effect; age and feature_a in particular show no movement the data can distinguish from zero."},{"id":6,"text":"The effect of utilization is broadly the same across different levels of delinquencies, income and history, so it acts as a fairly independent driver, whereas the interactions between delinquencies and debt-to-income, and between income and history, are small and modest in size."},{"id":7,"text":"Interactions are individually small compared with the main effects, and the data do not settle how much of their share of importance is real given the wide uncertainty bands."}]}
